prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "planbook", with the standing line "Turns a folder of loose origin notes into one Plan for a book, a single chapter table the scaffold can read." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows An open origins folder spills loose sheets of notes and research. One folder above it sits a single genre.yaml card. The sheets and the card are gathered, with a printed card of rules on top, into one bound prompt. A single arrow carries the prompt to the Anthropic model. One arrow leaves the model and ends at one finished Plan page. A faint thread of the origin sheets runs visibly into that page.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one shows the genre switch: genre.yaml tips the last table column toward Hidden Theme for an essay book or Subplot for a novel. circle two shows the rules card: one flat table of chapters, with no Parts or Sections. circle three shows --dry-run: the prompt printed on a page while the model stays untouched. study one shows --example, an existing Plan laid beside the prompt as a format guide. study two shows --spend, a dial set between cheap and pro. study three shows the cost ledger, one entry added per call.

Colour is used so that Vermilion marks origin material and every trace of it in the Plan. Blue marks the fixed house shape: the rules and the table structure. Ochre marks the genre choice.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: Four file types are read from the origins folder. The chapter table has six columns. Each row is one of three types: chapter, introduction, epilogue. Each run makes one model call. There are two spend tiers.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: origins sits on the folder. genre.yaml sits on the card above it. Thesis, Storyline, and Summary sit on the Plan's sections. On the table's column heads, # comes first, followed by Type, Slug, Title, Hook, and then Hidden Theme or Subplot. chapter, introduction, and epilogue sit on row types. --example sits on the reference Plan, --dry-run on the printed prompt, and --spend with cheap and pro on the dial. The cost ledger sits on the log book. scaffold sits on the next tool, which receives the Plan.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: origins folder, notes, research, genre.yaml, one prompt, Anthropic model, the Plan. essay book, novel, Hidden Theme, Subplot, --dry-run. --example, --spend, cheap or pro, cost ledger. Thesis, Storyline, chapter table, Hook, Summary, scaffold. read origins, load genre, build prompt, one call, write Plan.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Every note file read, subfolders included; genre.yaml sits one folder above. Genre picks the table's final column; Dry run prints the prompt, spends nothing. An existing Plan shows the house format; Every call logged with its cost. One flat table, no Parts or Sections; Every chapter rooted in the origins. Existing output overwritten with a warning.
